decision.rationale: PRR-018 is resolved and all existing exact-head tests and CI pass, but PRR-019 proves that a request can be written and flushed after its deadline while waiting for the worker lock, creating a retryable unknown outcome for a mutating action.

summary: The framing remediation correctly consumes readiness before dispatch and owns fd-level response framing. A newly identified concurrency boundary remains: the request deadline is fixed before lock acquisition but is not checked again before an action is written after the wait. Fix PRR-019 and add contention regressions before merge.

findings.title: Expired queued actions are dispatched before timeout is reported
findings.observation: run fixes its deadline before acquiring the worker lock, then calls _ensure_started and writes and flushes the request without rechecking the remaining budget. If lock waiting consumes the timeout, response reading immediately times out only after the request has crossed the dispatch boundary.
findings.trigger: Two threads share one ComputerUseMacOS instance and request A occupies the action worker longer than request B's timeout, so B acquires the lock after its own deadline.
findings.impact: B can perform an authorized but late UI mutation while the caller receives an unknown timeout result. Protocol timeouts are marked retryable, so a generic or manual retry can duplicate the side effect even though the internal action path does not replay it.

evidence.description: The deadline is created before the lock and no remaining-budget check exists before stdin.write and flush.
The protocol adapter classifies every TIMEOUT failure as retryable.

With timeout 0.1 seconds and the worker lock held for 0.2 seconds, exact-head code wrote one AXPress payload at 0.203 seconds, returned timed_out true, and failed a zero-write assertion with exit code 1.
The prior approved review contract treats write plus flush as potentially dispatched, making the post-deadline write an unknown mutating outcome.

findings.remediation: Acquire the worker lock using the remaining budget or check immediately after acquisition, check again after startup and readiness, and return timeout without writing or killing a healthy existing worker when the budget is exhausted.
findings.verification: Add a deterministic lock-contention test that asserts zero stdin writes after queue timeout and a slow restart or readiness variant that expires before dispatch; retain all framing, no-replay, package, repository, preflight, and CI gates.

findings.title: Warm worker could lose a buffered response and report a false timeout
findings.observation: The former select-before-TextIOWrapper.readline loop could hide a complete response in user-space buffering. The current implementation consumes readiness before dispatch and owns all stdout byte framing.
findings.trigger: A newly started worker emits readiness and handles a fast first query or action before the parent consumes readiness.
findings.impact: The previous code could falsely time out a query or report an executed action as unknown.

evidence.description: Startup waits for validated readiness and response reads consume an owned byte buffer before selecting and reading with os.read.
Real subprocess coverage includes coalesced frames, failed readiness, 100 immediate query responses, 100 immediate action responses, and dispatched-action timeout without replay.

findings.remediation: Completed: treat readiness as a startup handshake, use fd-level newline framing with an owned buffer, clean process resources, and preserve no replay after action dispatch.
findings.verification: Completed: original counterexample, real subprocess query and action stress, unknown-outcome no-replay, warning-as-error package tests, repository tests, packaging gates, and exact-head CI passed.

required_actions.action: Prevent worker dispatch after queue or startup consumes the request deadline, return timeout without disturbing a healthy worker, and add zero-write contention and slow-readiness regressions.
Repair readiness and response framing, add real subprocess protocol tests, and retain no replay after an unknown mutating outcome.

assumptions: A request timeout is a total caller budget including worker queue and startup time because the deadline is computed before lock acquisition.
A mutating request is potentially dispatched once write and flush are attempted, so subsequent failure must never trigger automatic replay.
Direct users may share a ComputerUseMacOS instance across threads and the worker lock is the serialization boundary for that use.
Newline-delimited UTF-8 remains the private worker protocol contract.
